unit.title: Colors and Describing Words: Los Colores

lesson.title: Es Rojo y Brillante: Describe the Mystery Object
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You can describe an object now. So can a friend — without telling you what it is. That is a riddle. 'Es rojo y brillante. ¿Qué es?' Today you guess, and you try to stump each other.

To describe one thing, start with es — it means 'it is.' Es rojo. Es grande. Join two describing words with y ('and'):

Es rojo y brillante.
Es azul y bonito.
Es pequeño y gris.

One new word made for riddles: [[brillante]] — bright or shiny. A new coin is brillante. A clean window is brillante. El sol es brillante. It ends in -e, so it never changes: el anillo es brillante, la estrella es brillante.

One player picks something in the room and describes it without naming it — a color plus one more word (brillante, grande, pequeño):

'Es blanca y grande. La maestra escribe aquí. ¿Qué es?' — La pizarra.
'Es pequeño y delgado. Tiene tinta azul. ¿Qué es?' — El bolígrafo.

Everyone guesses in Spanish: '¿Es la pizarra?' The first correct guess picks the next object.

Try these three. Say your answer out loud in Spanish before you read the next line.

1. Es amarillo y brillante. Da luz durante el día. ¿Qué es? (El sol.)
2. Es verde y pequeña. Sirve para dibujar líneas rectas. ¿Qué es? (La regla.)
3. Es gris o negra. Tiene una pantalla brillante. ¿Qué es? (La computadora.)
You described objects well enough to stump a friend — and you solved theirs. Tomorrow you write three describing sentences about your own favorite things.

questions.q: Es amarillo y brillante. Da luz y calor durante el día. ¿Qué es?
questions.explanation: El sol — yellow, bright, and it gives light and warmth by day. La luna (the moon) shines at night.

questions.q: Es blanca, grande y plana. La maestra escribe en ella. ¿Qué es?
questions.explanation: La pizarra — white, big, and flat, and the teacher writes on it. Blanca and plana end in -a to match la pizarra.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly joins two describing words?
questions.explanation: Start with es, then the first word, then y ('and'), then the second word: Es rojo y brillante.

questions.q: Mi mochila es morada y bonita. ¿De qué color es la mochila?
questions.explanation: Morada — purple. It ends in -a because mochila is a 'la' word: la mochila morada.

questions.q: Which is the correct Spanish word order?
questions.explanation: The describing word follows the noun: un bolígrafo brillante, just like un cuaderno rojo.

objectives: Describe an object with the frame es + color + y + a second word (Es rojo y brillante)
Use brillante correctly and know it never changes its ending
Solve and pose spoken riddles about classroom objects in Spanish
materialsNeeded: A handful of classroom objects to describe (notebook, pen, ruler, board, computer, eraser)
A partner or family member to trade riddles with
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's word order and agreement with two quick phrases: un cuaderno rojo, una regla verde.
2. Teach the frame es + word + y + word. Model three: Es grande y gris. Es pequeño y brillante. Es rojo y bonito.
3. Teach brillante (bright, shiny) with real examples — a coin, a window, a screen. Note it never changes.
4. Model a riddle: pick the ruler, say 'Es verde y pequeña. Sirve para dibujar líneas. ¿Qué es?' and have the child guess in Spanish.
5. Trade riddles back and forth about 5-6 objects. The child both guesses and poses.
6. Play the multiple-choice activity together.
7. Complete the worksheet.
8. Preview tomorrow: writing three describing sentences.
differentiationTips: Struggling: give the child three picture cards and let them pick which one matches each riddle you read, before asking them to pose their own
Ready for more: require three clues per riddle — a color, a size, and one of brillante/bonito/feo — and forbid pointing

For the teaching adult: 'es' here is the third-person singular of ser, taught as a fixed frame ('it is') per the course's band notes, not as a conjugation to drill. When an object's identity is still hidden, the masculine form is the default guess: 'Es rojo y brillante,' switching to -a once the answer (la manzana, la regla) is known
The riddle trade is a live spoken exchange, so it does not depend on the audio-recording gap noted elsewhere (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9)
teacherGuide.answerKey: Frame: es + color + y + second word — Es rojo y brillante. Brillante = bright/shiny, never changes. Practice riddles: 1. el sol, 2. la regla, 3. la computadora. Multiple-choice answers: 1. el sol, 2. la pizarra, 3. 'Es rojo y brillante', 4. morada, 5. un bolígrafo brillante. A well-formed riddle for el bolígrafo: 'Es pequeño y delgado. Escribes con él. ¿Qué es?'
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Day 3 in the scope-and-sequence is 'describe mystery objects — Es rojo y brillante. ¿Qué es?' Posing a riddle is presentational speaking (WA-WL-2015.1.3): the child produces a short, self-generated description for an audience and gets immediate feedback on whether it communicated. Solving the partner's riddle keeps interpretive listening active in the same activity. The es + color + y frame introduced here is the exact structure Thursday's written sentences and Friday's gallery presentation extend.
